logp.method_description: The partition coefficient (log P) was measured by flask shaking method. The compounds 2, 3 and 4 were pre-dissolved in DMF and then diluted in water to achieve 10-4 mol/L for 2 and 5·10-5 mol/L for 3 and 4 (for 3 and 4 the maximal concentration that could be achieved by this method), DMF concentration in water did not exceeded 0.2% v/v. Then, equal volumes (3 mL) of the aqueous solutions and n-octanol were mixed in 15 mL conical tubes, and shaken for 30 min at room temperature. Afterwards, the tubes were centrifuged to facilitate the separation of the layers. The aqueous layer was collected and the remaining complex concentration caqua was measured. Concentrations of the compounds were measured spectrophotometrically, at the respective absorption maxima, referenced to the calibration curves. The solutions obeyed Lambert-Beer’s law up to the maximal concentrations tested. The concentration coct of the compounds in n-octanol were calculated as follows: coct = ctotal - caqua. Log P was then calculated: log P = log coct - log caqua. The result is the mean from three replicates within standard deviation.
